title: Concurrent logins defeat the 5-failure account lockout through a lost-update on failed_logins
description: The per-account lockout is the only online-guessing brake on the admin login, and a trivial parallel request pattern fully defeats it: each concurrent wave of wrong-password requests advances the JavaScript-computed counter by about one.
root_cause: login reads the user row, checks locked_until on that stale copy, and writes failed_logins = user.failed_logins + 1 as an absolute value computed in JavaScript from the pre-read row (apps/admin/src/api.js:190-200). Concurrent wrong-password requests all read the same counter and each write the same +1, so LOCK_AFTER=5 is reached only after roughly 5 waves of any size. No IP throttle exists anywhere in the admin app or node-server.js.
intended_behavior: Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes (LOCK_AFTER=5, LOCK_SECONDS=900 at api.js:66-67), the documented anti-guessing control.

trace.description: Unauthenticated route, 4 KB body cap, no IP throttle.
SELECT reads the row; the lock check at 193-195 runs on this stale copy.
failed = user.failed_logins + 1 from the pre-read row, then an absolute UPDATE.
The 15 minute lock never engages under concurrency.

evidence.description: The read side of the read-modify-write.
Counter computed in JavaScript from the stale row.
Absolute UPDATE SET failed_logins = ? with the computed value.
Each guess still pays one 600,000-iteration PBKDF2 verify, bounding throughput but not the total guess count.

conditions.description: Unauthenticated internet user with a known admin email.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated attacker targeting a known admin email sends 5+ simultaneous wrong-password requests per wave; each wave advances the counter by about one while consuming many guesses, so the account never locks and guessing continues indefinitely at KDF speed.
payloads: 5+ concurrent POST /api/admin/login bodies with wrong passwords
instructions: Read the counter computation at api.js:197 and note it is JavaScript-side from the row read at 190
Send simultaneous wrong-password requests and observe failed_logins advances by about one per wave
execution.observed_result: Source-only analysis on this run: the read-modify-write is directly source-visible at the cited lines; no runtime execution was permitted on the Windows host.

remediation.strategy: Make the increment atomic in SQL: UPDATE admin_users SET failed_logins = failed_logins + 1, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_logins + 1 >= 5 THEN now + 900 END WHERE id = ? RETURNING failed_logins, locked_until, and gate the 401 on the returned values; optionally add a per-IP login throttle.

likelihood.reason: A trivial parallel request pattern defeats the only lockout control.

impact.reason: The lockout is fully defeated; guessing throughput remains bounded by the 600k-iteration KDF, so this matters against weak or leaked passwords.

confidence.reason: The counter computation and absolute write are directly source-visible; no runtime dependency.

title: First-admin setup code can be guessed without any limit during the bootstrap window
description: The setup code check has no throttle or counter and a non-constant-time compare, but the code carries roughly 40 bits of entropy in an 8-character alphanumeric code, and the window closes the moment the first admin exists, so online guessing is infeasible by many orders of magnitude.
claimed_root_cause: The setup code check in setupFirstAdmin has no throttle or attempt counter and compares with a plain inequality, so the code can be guessed online without limit.

trace.description: No counter, non-constant-time compare.
randomToken(6) filtered to alphanumerics, sliced to 8 characters, uppercased; on Render a fixed ADMIN_SETUP_CODE chosen by the owner is used instead.
Closes the moment the first admin exists.

evidence.description: The plain compare.
randomToken from crypto.getRandomValues.
The code is nulled after success.

reason: The factual observations hold (no throttle, non-constant-time compare), but the exploit is infeasible: the target is an 8-character alphanumeric code with roughly 40 bits of entropy (on Render a fixed ADMIN_SETUP_CODE chosen by the owner instead), the endpoint disappears the moment the first admin is created, a window of minutes on a fresh deploy, and even ignoring the window, unlimited online guessing at 100 requests per second needs centuries to cover the space, while the window itself allows only a few thousand guesses. An attacker who somehow won would create an account the owner discovers immediately. This is a hardening note (constant-time compare plus a small failure counter would be tidy), not a vulnerability.

title: Replayed contact step re-arms failed delivery channels and swaps the destination
description: A placement attempt holder can replay the contact step: each replay rewrites the attempt's email and WhatsApp and re-arms any channel whose previous send failed, producing another school-branded result message to a newly chosen address for as long as the sends keep failing.
root_cause: saveContact rewrites attempts.name/email/whatsapp unconditionally and re-arms a channel whenever its sent_at is NULL (apps/web/src/api.js:575-579), while delivery.js writes sent_at only on success (packages/core/src/delivery.js:94,103), so a failed channel keeps NULL sent_at, flips back to pending on replay, and the same handler then calls deliverInBackground (api.js:594), which sends to the freshly written destination. The student_id is immutable after the first contact (api.js:571), so only the delivery destination moves.
intended_behavior: The documented intent: a failed channel is retried after the student corrects the address, and a delivered channel is never sent twice. The residual defect is that nothing bounds retry frequency and the destination is rewritable by the attempt holder.

title: Mockup speaking re-upload resets tries and re-queues Speechace without bound, with no duration gate
description: Any invited mockup participant can re-upload a 1KB junk recording any number of times, including after all three Speechace tries failed, because the upsert resets tries to 0 for pending and failed rows, and each upload fires a fresh paid Speechace call.
root_cause: uploadMockupSpeaking's ON CONFLICT clause resets tries=0, lease_until=0, next_attempt_at=0 and clears error/scores for any row in status pending or failed, then immediately fires gradeMockupAnswer (apps/web/src/api.js:711-719). The worker's MAX_TRIES=3 cap bounds tries only within a single arm, never across re-arms, because the route zeroes tries with no counter or cooldown. The route also stores x-duration with no validation at all (line 703). The placement route shows the intended gates: clamped duration and replace-only-while-pending-tries-0-lease-expired (api.js:662-682).
intended_behavior: Re-recording replaces the audio only while the answer is still pending or failed, and the Speechace queue tries each answer at most MAX_TRIES times before waiting for the team.

title: Uncapped violation logging appends to an unbounded TEXT column with whole-row rewrites
description: The violation endpoint accepts unlimited POSTs per in-progress attempt, each appending a fixed small entry to violation_log, with the row surviving until the sweep at expires_at+60, so a scripted holder can bloat one row and amplify writes quadratically.
root_cause: logViolation gates only the type whitelist and status in_progress, and appends violation_log = COALESCE(violation_log,'') || entry with no count or length ceiling (apps/web/src/api.js:294-306). The client-side debounce and limit dialog are client-only; the server keeps accepting violations on a paused attempt because the limit no longer ends anything server-side. Postgres MVCC rewrites the whole row per append, so n appends of a growing column cost O(n^2) bytes.
intended_behavior: The server records each focus violation as a fixed small entry so the dashboard can show strike history; the cap exists in the runner, not the server.

execution.attacker_perspective: A scripted holder of their own attemptId loops the violation POST; each call appends and rewrites the row. Self-inflicted on their own row, but it degrades the shared database.

remediation.strategy: Cap the log (keep the last 50 entries) and stop counting or appending once violations exceeds max_violations, so a flood costs the attacker more than the server.

impact.reason: DB bloat and write amplification on one own row for one test's lifetime; no cross-tenant effect.

confidence.reason: The verifier downgraded the severity from medium and confirmed the mechanism; the window and principal bound the impact.
